analysis.title: Systematic Flows Monitor: Tech selloff drives CTA de-risking, with further equity selling still possible
key_insights: BofA's model shows CTAs sold equities this week as trends weakened, volatility rose and stop-loss thresholds were crossed. Friday's tech-led selloff likely drove significant de-risking in S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures.

Exhibit 12 shows no full S&P 500 model stop-outs, but weaker trends and higher realized vol likely cut exposure substantially. CTAs may keep some S&P 500 length but should stay biased toward selling next week.

A further 2% decline in the S&P 500 would fully unwind the remaining CTA longs, and the selling itself could speed up the move lower. The model's S&P 500 sell trigger starts at 7,606 against a current 7,617.

Faster CTA models may already be short Russell 2000 and EURO STOXX 50 futures and could turn short elsewhere on further declines. Slower models, where BofA believes most AUM sits, need more time for trends to erode.

Systematic strategies across CTAs, risk parity and vol control could sell $63bn in a down market, sell $15bn if flat, and buy $37bn in an up market over the next week. Positioning across the three is now above its five-year median.
The US would lead equity selling in the bear path, and selling from vol control could add to CTA unwinds on the downside.

Treasury futures trends are moving away from maximum negative levels after 10yr yields fell for a fourth week. CTAs remain far from long. Some TU and FV shorts may remain, while TY and longer-duration shorts have already stopped out.
Outside the US, KTB positioning is mixed across trend horizons, while CTAs remain firmly long Chinese 10yr bond futures.

CTA positioning is still broadly long USD after a slight dollar gain this week. The EUR short is the most stretched FX position, GBP strength has moved some models closer to stop-outs, and projections point to AUD buying and MXN selling.

Gold shorts are approaching the stretched levels last seen in August. Crude oil longs remain stretched with sell triggers more than 11% away. Aluminum shorts are elevated versus history, with the first buy-to-cover trigger roughly 1% away.
Soybean and soybean meal longs continued to stop out, and soybean oil selling is also possible next week.

SPX hedger gamma ended 29-Oct at $7.1bn (73rd percentile in the last year). With SPX down 1.82% and the VIX near 24 intraday on 30-Oct, hedger gamma could fall and even turn negative if spot keeps dropping.
Gamma expiring on FOMC Wednesday (28-Oct) was positive but small at $0.14bn. Gamma from 1DTE option selling flow was muted, though deep OTM 1DTE vertical spread selling persisted daily.
Averaged intraday over 5 days, delta-hedgers were net long $6.6bn of SPX gamma, split $2.6bn non-expiring, $2.3bn 0DTE and $1.7bn expiring open interest.

US leveraged and inverse ETFs would need to trade about $1.1bn of S&P 500 and $2.5bn of Nasdaq-100 per 1% move into the close. That is 3% and 21% of average 3:55-4:00 PM notional in ES and NQ futures and QQQ.

Single-stock leveraged ETF rebalancing is largest in TSLA (about $105mn per 1% move, 6.9% of late-session notional) and NVDA (about $88mn, 2.1%). Tesla and NVIDIA have the largest leveraged ETF AUM at about $4.4bn and $3.9bn.

macro_indicators.reading: Declined for a fourth consecutive week
macro_indicators.interpretation: Treasury futures trends are moving off maximum negative levels, but CTAs remain far from establishing longs.
Tech-led selloff on underwhelming tech results and AI fears drove CTA de-risking and pushed the VIX near 24 intraday.

risk_factors: Further equity declines could trigger mechanical CTA selling that accelerates the move lower.
Vol control selling could add to CTA unwinds in a down market.
Hedger gamma could turn negative if SPX keeps falling, which would amplify moves.
Leveraged and inverse ETF end-of-day rebalancing can amplify index and single-stock moves into the close.
CTA trigger levels vary by model construction, so actual flow timing and size may differ from BofA's single-model estimates.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 projects systematic strategies selling $63bn in a down market, selling $15bn if flat and buying $37bn in an up market over the next week.
Exhibit 11 lists S&P 500 futures trend strength of 18% short term, 91% medium term and 100% long term, with a sell trigger at 7,606.
Exhibit 63 states leveraged and inverse ETFs need to trade approximately $1.1bn per 1% S&P 500 move, about $16mn less than last week.
Exhibit 64 states leveraged and inverse ETFs need to trade approximately $2.5bn per 1% Nasdaq-100 move, about $120mn less than last week.
vol_and_positioning: The VIX neared 24 intraday on 30-Oct as SPX fell 1.82%.
SPX delta-hedger gamma ended 29-Oct at $7.1bn (73rd percentile in the last year) and could fall and flip negative if spot keeps declining.
If delta-hedging were confined to the last 15 minutes of the session, SPX gamma may have cut S&P 500 e-mini 1-month realized vol by 1.3 pts (11%) over the past month.
CTA model S&P 500 trend strength is +18% short term, +91% medium term and +100% long term. Nasdaq-100 is +9%, +61% and +93%. Russell 2000 short-term trend is -100%.
CTA positioning: EUR/USD at -100% across all three trend windows, oil at +100% across all windows, and 10yr Treasury futures at -100% on medium and long windows.
Systematic equity positioning across CTAs, risk parity and vol control is above its five-year median, using assumed assets of $300bn in CTAs and $200bn each in risk parity and vol control.

tension_points.bull_case: In an up market CTAs could reload on equities and systematic strategies could buy $37bn over the next week.
tension_points.bear_case: In a down market systematic strategies could sell $63bn, with vol control selling adding to CTA unwinds and hedger gamma possibly turning negative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The S&P 500 futures sell trigger at 7,606 and a further 2% decline that would fully unwind remaining CTA longs.
